headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure and capacity auctions from residential ratepayers to large energy users like data centers.
status: Last Action: Governor's Action Deadline 11:59 p.m., May 23, 2026 on 2026-04-22
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Dominion Energy (initially).
news_headline: Virginia governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger suggested amendments to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aimed to shift energy costs onto data centers and large manufacturers to save residential customers money. Her amendments removed the direct cost shift for purchasing additional power, instead allowing the State Corporation Commission to determine fair share payments, which critics argue weakens the bill's original intent.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water users providing water to data centers to report their total water volume, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, Potomac Conservancy, local communities, water conservationists.
news_headline: Data centers are drinking our Potomac River region resources up. Our team is fighting for transparency in Virginia
news_summary: Potomac Conservancy is advocating for SB 553, a bill that requires data centers to report their water usage to the State Water Control Board. This transparency is crucial for environmental advocates to understand and address the impact of data center sprawl on the Potomac River region's water supply, which faces potential failure by 2030 due to drought conditions.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill addresses community concerns by establishing regulations for data center siting and setting limits on noise generation.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data center sites, Del. Joshua Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (implied).
news_headline: As data center noise concerns grow, Loudoun Co. officials discuss possible mitigation efforts
news_summary: Residents in Loudoun County are experiencing constant, high-pitched noise from a data center that generates its own power, leading to headaches and sleep disturbances. While the data center claims compliance, the county's current noise ordinance doesn't measure tonal noise, prompting officials to explore legislative avenues to address these growing community concerns.
